Firebreak 0.4.0 is an early development build: stages 1 and 2 of a planned twelve (River Village and Dune Sea). Linux x86-64, OpenGL 3.3-compatible graphics. This release is marked as a pre-release.

- Stage 2, Dune Sea, is playable: high noon over dunes, an oasis and a mud-brick village. Militia in shemaghs, rooftop snipers, camel scouts, a pickup technical with a bed gunner, and a convoy truck mid-boss. No helicopter on this stage.
- After you clear River Village, the travel map continues into Dune Sea. Clearing Dune Sea previews Coral Coast as coming soon.
- Heat shimmer on the desert panorama, and a short dust-storm beat near the village.
- Dates, bread and a waterskin drop as health pickups. Robed adult civilians still cost a penalty.
- Stage 2 music and desert effects are third-party CC0 recordings (see NOTICE): Darbuka Delight by Adiutorium, Desert Loop by iamoneabe as a backup, plus truck, wind, gust, camel and falling-brick sounds. No new ElevenLabs audio.
- Campaign scoring is unchanged. The optional global top 100 still ranks one campaign score, with a 40,000-point cap per stage.
- The Godot app icon uses the same palette-quantised 512 px artwork as the store listing, under the Snap Store's 256 kB limit.

Download `Firebreak-0.4.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, extract it and run `Firebreak/play.sh`. A `.deb` and an AppImage are also attached. Confirm the files against `SHA256SUMS-0.4.0`. Godot is not required. A Windows zip may be attached for testing; it has not been run on Windows and is not supported.

The Snap Store package is `firebreak-game`. A tag push uploads it to the `edge` channel; promoting a revision to `stable` is done by hand. Version 0.3.7 remains on `edge` as revision 2 until this build replaces it.

Only stages 1 and 2 are playable. Testing was on Linux x86-64 with Intel Mesa graphics; no physical gamepad was connected. The optional global top 100 cannot be verified — the game is open source, so fake scores remain possible. The ElevenLabs plan behind the older bundled audio is not yet confirmed; see NOTICE.

Source and original artwork: Apache-2.0. Bundled fonts, music, speech and effects retain the terms in NOTICE.
